subtitle: إتقان — daily tasks, habits and long-term goals in one calm place
next_actions: New: Settings opens one section at a time — a side menu on the laptop, a list on the phone — so nothing is a long scroll away.

New: Itqan now announces each update in a 'What's new' window when you open it (once per device); Settings → What's new lists them all. Also: a guide and checklist when you create a goal, and clearer on/off switches on notes.

New: counted habits (pages, minutes…) show their totals in Insights → Amounts, against the previous period. Edit a counted habit to give it a full round — e.g. 604 pages and the page you're on — and it shows Round 1 · 250/604 and roughly when you'll finish; a finished round starts the next. Open Itqan on the iPhone once so it updates (data format v15); sync resumes after that.

To do (owner): deploy the push relay once so browser installs (your friend's Edge on Windows) can send focus endings to a phone — run relay/deploy.sh, then set the repo variable PUSH_RELAY_URL (steps in relay/README.md).

New: Notes (in the menu after Ideas, key 9). Type a line and press Enter to save a note, or start a checklist. Pin, colour and label notes, search them, archive the ones you're done with. Any note or checklist line can become a task. Projects and goals show their notes too, and in Ctrl+K, 'note: …' saves one. To keep a note on Today, open it and tap the sun; tap the sun on its card on Today to take it off. Open Itqan on the iPhone once so it updates (data format v14); sync resumes after that.

New: streak savers. Every 500 XP earns one (you can hold 2); a missed day uses one by itself and your streak on Today survives. Tap the flame on Today to see your savers, the last four weeks and how it works. Your existing history counts, so you may already hold some.

Reminders and check-ins with people now reach the iPhone as notifications, even with Itqan closed there (the laptop sends them, so it needs to be awake). Open Itqan on the iPhone from the Home Screen once so it updates (data format v12); sync resumes after that.
If 'Alerts from my laptop' isn't on yet on the iPhone: Settings → Notifications → turn it on and allow once. The switches above it (focus endings, reminders, check-ins) choose what the phone gets.
Insights has a new Focus section and compares every number with the previous period — pick 7, 14, 30 or 90 days at the top. Tap a bar on the phone to see its value.
Focus can now be for a habit: pick it on Focus, or press the timer on a habit card. Finishing checks the habit in — its minutes for a minutes habit (e.g. "10 min"), otherwise one check.
Training → Routines → Program now offers "Whenever I can" (no schedule). Fixed days and Rotation still work as before.
Number keys: 7 Training, 8 Ideas, 9 Notes (Reminders no longer has a number key — use Ctrl+K or the menu).
In Settings → Profile, pick your interface language (it follows you to your other devices). All four translations have had their independent review (S2-23); if a phrase still reads oddly, note it.
Record this year's achievements so far; check the suggestions Itqan offers.

log.entry: S2-50 (ADR-042), asked for by the owner: Settings was one long scroll (profile, day start, notifications, daily card, areas, sync, data, shortcuts) and easy to get lost in. Now eight sections, each at #/settings/<section>: on a laptop a sticky side menu beside the open section (General by default); on a phone #/settings is a list with one-line hints and a section opens alone with a back link. Language got its own card at the top of General. Links into Settings now land on the right section (daily card gear → Daily card, notification hints → Notifications, backup reminder → Backup and data, onboarding's sync → Sync, Notifications' 'needs sync' → a link to Sync). No data change. Checked in the browser at 1280 and 375 px, light and dark, English and Arabic.

S2-49 (ADR-041), asked for by the owner: an optional rule that a day starts at Fajr instead of midnight, so work after midnight but before Fajr counts for the day before. Off by default. Dated as fajrSpans (schema v16, migration + tests): switching on, off or moving never re-dates anything already done — the owner's explicit worry for existing users — tested with XP, the day streak and day counts identical across a switch. dayOf()/todayKey() read the spans; every instant-to-day read goes through them, and a source guard fails CI on a new toKey(new Date(...)). Fajr maths in lib/fajr.ts (no dependency), within 2 min of the adhan library across seven cities; place from the device time zone's city or coordinates, angle by local authority. Spans sync one entity each so a stale device cannot wipe them. A toast after completing a task or habit says which day it counted for. Checked in the browser at 1:33 AM Cairo: Today showed Tuesday, a task and a habit landed on the 27th, switching back moved nothing; Arabic layout checked.

S2-46…48, asked for by the owner. S2-46: the On Today switch showed the dim sun when on (reads as off) and both suns look alike; note switches now show their state — filled icon on a green chip when on, outline when off. S2-47 (ADR-039): the goal editor gets a folding 'How to set a good goal' panel (do's and avoids), a live checklist — Specific, Measurable, Deadline, Why (goalChecks, 8 tests) — and the pace the deadline asks; advice only. S2-48 (ADR-040): What's new — release notes in src/content/releases.ts (five languages) shown once per device after an update, history in Settings; releases.test.ts fails CI when a done task is unannounced, so it is now part of shipping (CLAUDE.md rule 9). Checked in the browser, English and Arabic.

S2-45, asked for by the owner: Insights counts the pages, minutes, reps… of every counted habit — the period's amount vs the period before, the mean a day and the all-time total (habitAmounts). And an optional round per counted habit (Habit.round, schema v15, migration 14 → 15 gives none, tested): the editor asks the size and where you are now; rounds wrap (a habit goes on); the finish date comes from the last 28 days' pace. Shown on the Habits row and in Insights → Amounts. 20 new tests; five languages; checked in the browser.

S2-44, reported by the owner for a friend on Windows/Edge: focus endings never reached the iPhone and the device test button was missing. Cause: only the Linux app's desktop helper sends pushes, and Apple/Google push services refuse requests from web pages (no CORS — checked). Fix (ADR-037): a Cloudflare Worker push relay (relay/) with the helper's guards (relay/guard.ts, 8 tests); browser installs send timer endings and test pushes through it; Settings says plainly when a device can't send. Verified: real Chrome subscription → push.ts → relay → Google push service 201. Waiting on the owner to deploy the Worker (relay/deploy.sh) and set PUSH_RELAY_URL. Also: a regression test for tick → untick → tick (habitRetick.test.ts) — the reported 2-day streak could not be reproduced; asked the owner for details.

S2-43, asked for by the owner: a gear at the daily card's bottom start corner (bottom-left; bottom-right in Arabic) opens Settings at #/settings/daily, which scrolls to the daily card section and marks it briefly. Card now takes a ref; label in five languages. Checked in the browser.

S2-42, asked for by the owner: pin a note to the home screen (ADR-036). A separate switch, Note.onToday (schema v14, migration 13 → 14 puts no existing note on Today, tested), so pinning to the top of Notes doesn't crowd Today. Set with the sun button in the note editor; Notes cards show an 'On Today' mark. Today shows them first in the side column, under the daily card (on a phone, straight after the tasks — never above them, ADR-023), as full cards: lines tick in place, the card opens the editor, and 'Remove from Today' has Undo. Order is creation (todayNotes() in lib/notes.ts, tested) so ticking never reorders. 5 new tests; five languages; checked in the browser at desktop and 375 px.

S2-41, asked for by the owner: a note keeper (ADR-035). He chose Keep-style cards linked to the rest of Itqan. New Note entity (schema v13, migration 12 → 13 with tests): title, text and/or a checklist, colour from the area palette, labels, pinned, archived, optional area / project / goal. Notes screen after Ideas: one-line capture, new checklist, search (every word, any case or accent), label chips, Notes / Archive, Pinned and Others in columns; cards tick lines, pin and archive in place with Undo. The editor is opened from anywhere, saves on close (an empty new note is not created) and is remounted per opening — in testing, resetting the draft in an effect let an old note's text into a new one, which would have saved a duplicate. A note or one line becomes a task keeping its area / project / goal; the line counts as done once the task is (derived). Project pages and goal details list and add their notes; Ctrl+K saves 'note: …' (colon required) and opens a new note. Pure logic in lib/notes.ts; 16 new tests (filtering, labels, checklist progress, conversions, store actions, unlinking on delete, sync round trip, migration, quick add in five languages). Five languages; checked in the browser at desktop and 375 px, light and dark, English and Arabic (RTL) — labels isolated with <bdi> there, which also fixes the same # placement on Memories tags. Number key 9 is now Notes.

S2-40, asked for by the owner: streak savers, like Duolingo's streak freeze (ADR-034). Every 500 XP earns one, at most 2 held; a missed day is covered automatically and the day streak on Today lives on (a covered day doesn't add to the count). A gap longer than the savers held ends the streak but keeps the savers. Everything is derived from the XP history by dayStreak() in lib/gamification.ts (replaces activeStreak; 17 tests: earning, the cap, gaps, today pending, backfilling returning a saver, order independence) — no schema change, nothing synced. The flame on Today now shows savers and opens a dialog (streak, best, savers with progress, last four weeks, how it works); a line on Today when savers just covered the days before, or in the evening with none left; a toast when one is earned; savers held in Insights. The active-14 badge now reads the best run, so it is never taken back. Also: useProgress now recomputes when workouts change (training XP was missed until something else changed). Five languages; checked in the browser at desktop and 375 px, light and dark, English and Arabic (RTL).

S2-39, asked for by the owner: notifications for check-ins and reminders. On the laptop they already arrived (helper, even with the app closed); on the iPhone only while Itqan was open, because pushes carried timer ends only. Now the laptop pushes reminders and check-ins to every registered phone that wants that kind (ADR-033). PushTarget gains `kinds`, mirroring the phone's own switches (schema v12, migration tested; existing registrations get every kind until the phone narrows them). Pushes are built for the coming 7 days; a reminder or check-in may still go out up to 12 hours late (helper v3, `pushLateMs`, capped and tested); pushed text is clipped and at most 10 devices per alert, so one long note can never make the helper refuse the whole schedule. A push and the phone's own in-app alert share a tag, so they never stack.

S2-38, asked for by the owner: Insights was rebuilt (ADR-032). The range (7/14/30/90 days) now scopes the whole screen and every headline number — XP, tasks, focus time, habit consistency — shows its change against the previous period, a trend line and its all-time total. A new Focus section: total, sessions, average session, daily average, focus days, focus streak (current and best); focus time per day with an average line; when you focus (by hour, peak marked); average by weekday (strongest marked); by area (share bar and table); what the time went to (by habit, goal or label); session-length bands; records (longest session, best day). The activity heatmap switches between XP and focus. Maths in lib/insights.ts with 20 tests (late-night sessions, hours past midnight, weekday averages, streak edges, habits created later); charts hand-drawn, no new dependency. Checked in the browser at 1280 and 375 px, light and dark, English and Arabic (RTL).

S2-37, asked for by the owner: the 'allow notifications?' prompt appeared on every focus start — the laptop app is a file:// page, where Chrome never keeps the grant, and Focus asked each time. Now nothing asks on start; Settings → Notifications is the one place: allow once (phone/browser), a master switch and switches for focus/break endings, reminders and check-ins, per device. And a session that ends on the laptop is pushed to the iPhone: the phone turns on 'Alerts from my laptop', sync carries its registration to the laptop, the laptop signs and encrypts a Web Push for it, and the desktop helper (v2) sends it when the timer ends — no server, no new account (ADR-031, schema v11). Encryption matches the RFC example byte for byte; a real push went through Google's push service into Chrome. Not yet seen on the iPhone itself.

S2-36, asked for by the owner: on the phone the floating + always opened a new task, even on Habits. Each screen now says what its + adds (ADR-030): a habit on Habits, a goal on Goals, a project, a reminder, a person (or a check-in on a person's page), a memory, an achievement; on Ideas it jumps to the capture line; on a project's page it adds a task already in that project. Today, Plan, Focus and Review keep the new task; Training, Insights and Settings have no +. The button shows the screen's icon with a small + so the change is visible. Phone only — desktop has no floating button. Checked on every screen at phone width.

S2-35, reported by the owner: a focus session ended and no notification came, though notifications had been allowed. Only the page announced a timer's end, with a browser notification, and from the file:// app that never reached the desktop (Chrome asked for permission but kept no grant in the profile). The running timer's end now goes on the desktop helper's schedule like a reminder (ADR-013, amended), so it arrives even with Itqan minimised or closed; pausing or stopping early takes it off, and a timer that ran out stays on long enough for the helper to fire it. No duplicate from the page while the helper is connected. Tested, including that the guard against the finish-then-resync race fails when removed.

S2-34, a day-boundary fix: a habit's history started on the UTC day of its creation, so a habit made between midnight and 03:00 here began the day before and counted that day as missed in its streak periods, rates and the weekly review. It now starts on the local day; the same slip in a project's pace (no start date set) is fixed too. Tests build the creation time from a local just-after-midnight and just-before-midnight, so they fail on the old code on either side of UTC. No other place in the code takes a day from an ISO timestamp.

S2-33, at the owner's request: a focus session can be for a habit (ADR-029). Pick a habit on Focus or press the new timer button on a habit card; finishing logs it on the session's start day — its minutes when the habit is counted in minutes (units recognised in all five languages), otherwise one check-in — and deleting the session takes back exactly that. Deleting a habit unlinks its sessions and keeps their minutes. Schema v10 (sessions and a running timer gain habitId: null). Tested (late-night day, take-back never below zero, discard and breaks add nothing, migration, backup), checked in the browser.

S2-32, at the owner's request: training without a schedule. A third program mode, "Whenever I can" — now the default for anyone new — where nothing is due or missed: Overview and Today say "Ready when you are" and suggest the routine you've left longest (never-done first), with "last done …" and "Last workout: …" as plain information; an optional weekly aim (0 = none). Schema v9 changes no data; it makes a not-yet-updated device pause sync instead of misreading the mode. Tested (suggestion order, unfinished workouts ignored, the migration, the new default), checked in the browser in English and Arabic. Also: finished work is now pushed and installed without asking (memory/09-workflow.md).

S2-31: independent review of every new Training string in Arabic, French, Chinese and Spanish (62 lines in 24 files). Main fixes: Arabic no longer uses تمرين (exercise) for the program and says إلغاء, not تجاهل, for discarding a workout; "plan" words that clashed with the Plan screen became program words in ar/es/zh; the weekly-review label under the workout count now reads right under any number in ar/fr/es; French no-break spaces between numbers and units; gender-neutral French badge titles; one word for Resume and for each record type throughout. Left as is: Spanish Gemelos (Spain/anatomical), English gym words French and Spanish lifters use (Hip thrust, Dips), the long Arabic 1-rep-max label.

S2-28 to S2-30: the Training screen. Overview (today's routine from the program, resume, start another or an empty workout, this week vs plan with sets per muscle, recent workouts), History (month calendar, any day's workouts with every set and PRs, any exercise's records and chart), Routines (program by fixed days or rotation, times per week, linked habit; routine editor with per-measure targets), Exercises (editor, search, archive, "Add common exercises" in the interface language). The live workout: one exercise at a time, target, last time, next-time suggestion, set rows prefilled so logging is one tap on Easy/Good/Hard/Failed, rest timer, add/reorder/skip, finish summary with records and XP, resumes after reload, keeps the phone screen on. Elsewhere: a Training card on Today, goals that follow an exercise's best or count workouts, kg/lb in Settings, workouts and records in the weekly review, start/resume from Ctrl+K. Tabs built by the builder subagent (Sonnet), live workout and connections in the main session; checked in the browser at 375 px and desktop, light and dark, English and Arabic.

S2-27: Training maths in src/lib/training.ts, all tested — what is due (weekdays; rotation replays history so a skipped day waits and A B A C works), last time (same routine slot), next-time suggestion (+1 step when every set hit the top at Easy/Good, −1 after failures two workouts running), records (heaviest, reps, 1RM, volume, reps at each weight; warm-ups never count; a first attempt is no record), workout and week summaries, weeks-on-plan. Goals can follow an exercise's best or count workouts (derived, so deleting a workout can't leave a stale number). Workouts earn 30 XP (+10 per record, max 3); five new badges in all five languages. Each guard was checked by breaking it and seeing a test fail.

S2-26: data format v8 for Training — exercises, routines, program, workouts and sets (sets as their own collection so two devices logging one workout keep every set), Goal.link, Settings.weightUnit (kg). The upgrade adds only empty collections and defaults; tested from v7 data and a v7 backup, through sync (program absent until saved, so a fresh device stays fresh), and every store action incl. the linked-habit tick and its undo. Nothing visible yet.

Training (exercise and gym tracking), at the owner's request: spec agreed in chat and kept in memory/11-training.md — exercises, routines, a program by weekdays or rotation (customizable), live workouts with last time, effort per set, rest timer and suggestions, PRs, history by day and exercise, kg by default, logging on laptop and phone. Decision record ADR-027; built as S2-26 to S2-31.

S2-25, from the owner's report: "New goal" on the Goals page closed without creating anything — since the first commit. Cause: the editor saved with onCreated?.(add(goal)), and an optional call skips its arguments when there is no callback, which is exactly the Goals page (Plan and Projects passed one, so it worked there). Fixed, and src/lib/__tests__/sourceGuards.test.ts now fails on any optional call with a call in its arguments. Also at the owner's request: goal cards are about half as tall — progress ring, title, area and pace, one line of facts, and a quick + (numeric) or the next milestone to tick; the whole card opens a details dialog with the why, all milestones, the progress history and every action (ADR-026). Checked in the browser at 375 and 1280 px, light and dark, English and Arabic.

S2-24, at the owner's request: the onboarding starter set no longer mirrors his own routine (this repository is public). It is now a generic example in all five languages — Health, Mind, Learning, Books, Work, Life; habits like Drink water, Read, Meditate, Exercise; goals Read 12 books, Run 5 km, Learn a new skill, Finish an online course. Onboarding text, quick-add examples and memory/00-project.md follow suit; the routine is kept only in the private, local notes. Existing data is untouched — the starter set is only created at first run (ADR-025).

Phone navigation, at the owner's request: the bottom bar's fifth item is now More (the menu) instead of Focus; the sheet it opens lists Projects, Focus, Ideas and every other screen. The header's menu button is gone (it duplicated More). A running focus timer shows as a dot on More and a countdown on the Focus tile, so it isn't hidden behind the menu.

S2-23: independent review of every translation against its language guide, one reviewer for the screens and one for the daily-card content per language, language by language — Arabic 87 fixes, French 53, Chinese 56, Spanish 59 (meaning, calques, grammar, glossary consistency, hadith checked against the Arabic, Chinese-word definitions that were only synonyms, Spain-only words in Spanish, one Quran excerpt re-cut). Code fixes the reviewers found: signed numbers (“+5 XP”) kept their sign in front in right-to-left; “None” in pickers per thing picked (gender in French/Spanish); “every week” no longer “every 1 week” in Chinese (tested); a project with no tasks gets its own delete confirmation; habit streak labels read right under any number; GitHub’s English-only labels quoted as they are; the English of Bukhari 3559 now says “Among the best of you”. Rules added to memory/10-localization.md.

S2-07: Itqan in English, Arabic (right to left), French, Chinese and Spanish (ADR-024, schema v7) — every screen, quick add (day words per language, tested), and the daily card (published Quran meanings for French/Spanish/Chinese, verified; hadith, wisdom, facts and 1,000 word meanings translated). Automated translation checks for completeness, placeholders, plural forms, typography and leftover English all pass. The independent per-language review was stopped before it finished and is follow-up S2-23.

S2-00 follow-up: install_local.sh now runs `npm ci` whenever package-lock.json is newer than npm's record of the last install, so `git pull` + the script is the whole update — before, a pull that added a package (ADR-023's font) broke the build until a manual `npm install`. `npm ci`, not `npm install`: it never rewrites tracked files that would block the next pull. Checked: up to date → skipped; changed lockfile → installed; checkout stays clean.
